prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro: urban CBTC railway (peak/off-peak/engineering hours); separation, MA, regulation. Degraded: LTC declares when MA, localization, point detection, platform interface or radio untrusted; trains stationary or controlled speed until separation restored; restrictive platform states; explicit controller action before automatic departure. Triage classes: safety critical, service affecting, cyber, maintenance-only; safety critical stays under traffic control until LTC confirms restriction and Maple confirms engineering status. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (LTC; OCC; selects holding/skip-stop/turnback/run-through via Lantern; produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice; station holds without route-locking change; no vital intervention; verifies revised timetable; receives Route Release Exception List; fault summaries only). Revenue Train Operator (acknowledgements to Atlas; repeats back Voice Dispatch Console instructions; reports via degraded-service channel; in restricted manual responsible for speed, stopping, door release, verbal limits). Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple (trends/faults/rejected commands from Maintenance Diagnostic Server; remote sessions read-only outside approved window; records track clearance). Cyber Security Officer (certificates, access logs, auth failures). Station staff. Elements: Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern (sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas; shall show affected limits, fallback mode, pending actions without obscuring safety alarms). Service Timetable Server, Passenger Information Gateway (publish after CBTC confirmation). Voice Dispatch Console (confirm/cancel distinct from timeout/failure). North District Zone Controller, alias Marble (East Junction; applies Temporary Speed Restriction Notice after validating limits against degraded-mode map); South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid (West Junction); send MA; handover validation; correspondence loss shortens MA. East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon (Axle Counter Reset Request); West Junction Interlocking (Route Release Exception List). Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel (modes incl. restricted manual when no valid MA or location confidence below threshold; Brake Curve Checksum Log). Dual Channel Odometer (channel disagreement → location uncertain). Train Radio Modem shall report safe-data loss to Atlas, not mask intermittent failures from cab; Wayside Radio Access Network, alias Saffron (failure: reduce throughput before manual working). Maintenance Diagnostic Server (cannot alter MA; preserves raw/normalised events, session notes, integrity values; evidence frozen, copied to protected repository). Configuration records: builds, parameters, radio, interlocking data, change refs. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance (certificate/key status).

New part:
S184: Orchid shall inhibit automatic route setting within any block whose occupancy state is under manual confirmation.
S185: The East Junction Interlocking shall hold commanded points locked until field confirmation or a verified diagnostic indication supports a safe release.
S186: The West Junction Interlocking shall reject a route command that conflicts with a manually protected train movement.
S187: Manual route recovery begins when the Line Traffic Controller confirms train positions through independent indications and direct verbal reports.
S188: Before a manual route is issued, the Signal Maintenance Engineer verifies point condition, track vacancy, and local protection using approved field procedures.
S189: The Signal Maintenance Engineer uses the Axle Counter Reset Request as the controlling authority for restoring a failed section after local occupancy checks are complete.
S190: Restricted manual movements shall be authorized through the Voice Dispatch Console unless the contingency communications procedure has been formally invoked.
S191: The Revenue Train Operator shall repeat back the movement limit, maximum permitted speed, stopping point, and any instruction to remain clear of a platform interface.
S192: The Platform Screen Door Controller remains in a protected local state when train stopping accuracy cannot be verified by the normal automatic interface.
S193: Reset authorizations require concurrence between the Line Traffic Controller and the Signal Maintenance Engineer when the reset can change route availability or occupancy status.
S194: Quarry shall mark each degraded-mode diagnostic session with the incident identifier before any component restart is attempted.
S195: The Cyber Security Officer shall review any degraded condition that involves authentication failure, unexpected lockout, or abnormal network access behavior.
S196: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance shall not be bypassed to accelerate service recovery unless the approved emergency security procedure is active.
S197: The Revenue Train Operator sends the Test Train Clearance Memo after completing the prescribed proving run under restricted manual control.
S198: The Passenger Information Gateway shall issue disruption messages that are consistent with the operating limits accepted by the Line Traffic Controller.
S199: Return to automatic operation requires stable communications, verified route state, confirmed train position, and a recorded handback from maintenance control to operations control.
S200: Cybersecurity controls for the Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System shall be treated as operating prerequisites for safe automatic train movement after any maintenance handback.
S201: The safety case assumes that loss of trust in communications can be as significant as loss of communications, and the operating response shall reflect that assumption.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
